title: Successive littoral explosions at the Puhi-o-Kalaikini ocean entry
place: Puhi-o-Kalaikini ocean entry, Kīlauea south coast, Hawaiʻi
notes: Zoomed view from the sea cliff: blue ocean, dark lava shoreline at bottom, a white steam column rising at right (x~0.75-1.0). Successive littoral explosions blast grey ash + black rock fragments up and out: first burst 1.0-2.5 s (x~0.5,y~0.5, rocks fly left), biggest blast 4.0-6.5 s with black rocks flung across the sky (x~0.2-0.5,y~0.1-0.6), smaller dark bursts ~8.5-9.5 s and ~11.5 s. Small white 'USGS' bug bottom-right (x~0.83-0.99,y~0.95) - crop away. Source 850x478 upscaled to 1920x1080 (soft). Best shot A 0.0-2.6 (steam -> first burst at 1.0); shot B 3.8-6.4 (big rock-throwing blast). Crop centre x~0.45.
fact_en: The explosions were throwing ejecta up to about 20 meters.
